# Bank Transfer Contract

Represents one payer-requested bank transfer with a separate guarantor confirmation. An unknown outcome is reconciled against the same request. Request acceptance does not confirm that money moved. This flow has no synthetic card authorization or capture; a refund is a separate transfer instruction.

## Terms and inputs

`paymentTerms.method` is `bank-transfer` and `paymentTerms.evidence` is `bankConfirmation`. `paymentTerms.amountMinor` supplies the full transfer amount in integer minor units of `paymentTerms.currency`. No amount, currency or channel defaults are established here.

`requestTransfer` is declared on channel `payer`; the three outcome operations are declared on `guarantor`. Their calling channels must also match `paymentTerms.payerChannel` and `paymentTerms.guarantorChannel`, respectively. Each first invokes `requireActive` with the calling channel; its detailed admission rules are not supplied.

Every transfer operation requires a text `requestId` of 1–128 characters. Outcome operations also require a text `reference` of 1–256 characters identifying the bank outcome. Identifiers are reused only for retries of the same transfer, and references are reused for retries of the same recorded outcome.

## Requesting the transfer

`requestTransfer` accepts only `requestId`; amount and currency come from `paymentTerms`.

- `/payment/accepted` must be exactly `true`.
- If `/clauses/documentSources` exists, `/sourceLinks/ready` must be exactly `true`.
- For a new request, `/payment/closed` must not be `true`. If `paymentTerms.transferGate` exists, it identifies a path in the executing document whose value must be exactly `true`.

When `/bankTransfer/requestId` is empty text, an admitted request records the identifier, sets `/bankTransfer/status` to `requested`, and emits a `Bank Transfer Event` with `kind: Transfer Requested`, `requestId`, `amountMinor` and `currency`. This records the request, not transferred money.

Once a nonempty identifier is recorded, another identifier is rejected with `BANK_REQUEST_CONFLICT`. Retrying the same identifier returns `duplicate` without issuing another transfer event. Earlier admission checks still apply, but this duplicate return precedes the closed-payment and transfer-gate checks.

## Recording the bank outcome

All three outcome operations require `requestId` to match the recorded nonempty `/bankTransfer/requestId`.

- `confirmTransfer` requires `requestId`, `reference`, `amountMinor` and `currency`. Amount and currency must exactly match the current `paymentTerms`. It records status `completed`, sets `/payment/completed` to the full configured amount, and sets `/payment/transactionId` to the bank reference. It emits `Payment Completed` carrying `amountCompleted`, `evidence: bankConfirmation`, `reference` and `requestId`. This is the transferred-money record for this flow.
- `declineTransfer` records status `declined`.
- `reportTransferUnknown` records status `unknown`, leaving the same request available for later confirmation or decline. Unknown does not mean failed or completed.

For decline and unknown outcomes, `amountMinor` and `currency` are optional. These handlers neither compare them with the terms nor store them. No other business fields are accepted. Decline and unknown do not change `/payment/completed` or `/payment/transactionId`.

Each newly accepted outcome updates `/bankTransfer/status` and `/bankTransfer/reference` and emits a `Bank Transfer Event` with `kind: Transfer Outcome`, `requestId`, `reference` and `status`.

A new outcome is allowed only from `requested` or `unknown`. Repeating the current status with the same reference returns `duplicate` without further state changes or events; repeating it with a different reference is rejected as `BANK_OUTCOME_CONFLICT`. Confirmation retries must still satisfy the amount and currency checks. A different status after `completed` or `declined` is rejected as `BANK_OUTCOME_FINAL`. Reconciliation from `unknown` to a final outcome may supply a new reference.

`acceptedNew` means the operation recorded a new request or outcome; only the confirmation branch records completion. Invalid fields, authority, identifiers, references, readiness or confirmation amounts/currency cause rejection.

## Inherited lifecycle and configuration

The type inherits Payment Instruction with Clauses. `acceptPaymentInstruction` is a guarantor operation accepting an empty object or optional text `reason`; `rejectPaymentInstruction` requires a nonempty `reason`. Other inherited payment and control response operations delegate to shared payment functions whose detailed guards and financial effects are not supplied. Their declarations alone do not establish another bank-transfer completion or refund mechanism.

`clauses` starts as an empty map. Clause initialization begins on `Document Processing Initiated`. Payment initialization is invoked after `Clauses Initialized` or `Document Activated` only when `/payment/accepted` is absent and either `/clauses/activation` is absent or `/activation/active` is `true`. The initializer's ledger defaults are not established here.

Inherited amendment processing checks `expectedRevision` and `expectedConfigurationId` against `/clauseRuntime/revision` and `/clauseRuntime/configurationId`, validates clause changes, and evaluates applicable transition and configuration hooks. A requested or prepared amendment is not an installed change: `Amendment Accepted` denotes installation, while `Amendment Rejected` preserves effective configuration and state.

All paths refer to the document executing this type. Missing state is unknown; it does not imply an empty request identifier, zero completed money, acceptance or a default status.
